Aerial Wildlife Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 354 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2023) 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit (WMU) 354 is a largely forested unit located in West-Central Alberta, covering an area 
of 2514 km2. It is bordered by the Forestry Trunk Road to the west, the Simonette River to the north, the Canfor 
7000 Road to the south, and by physical features and land survey boundaries along the east . In 1997, the unit 
was modified by splitting the combined boundary of what is now WMU 354 and 353, into two smaller units. The 
objective of this survey (2023) was to update the population estimate, and population ratio for sex and age 
classes for moose since the last survey in 2019.  
Survey Method 
The aerial survey for moose in WMU 354 was conducted between January 18th and 19th, 2023. Distance sampling 
methods (AEP 2016, Buckland et al., 2001) were used to determine moose population and density estimates.  
Transects (N = 142), up to 10 km in length and oriented north-south (Fig. 1), were established throughout the unit 
with 1.2 km spacing. A random sample (n = 81) of these transects was flown during this survey. Moose were 
classified by age (adult or young), sex, and antler class.  
Results 
The total survey effort included 716.8 km of transects, and approximately 17.8 hours of flight time. 
In total, 314 moose were included in the analysis from 209 independent groups observations. Of the 303 
successfully classified, 146 were cows, 79 were calves, and 78 were bulls. Of the bulls observed, 86% had 
already shed their antlers at the time of the survey. Of those with antlers (n=11), 82% were considered small 
(small spike or forked antlers) and 18% were considered medium (small palmated antler ‘paddles’).  The bull:cow 
and calf:cow ratios were 0.53 (95% CI 0.38 - 0.69) and 0.54 (95% CI 0.46 – 0.63), respectively. The density 
estimate was 1.18 moose/km2 (90% CI 1.02-1.37) with a coefficient of variation (CV) of 9.01%. The estimated 
moose population for WMU 354 is 2976 (90% CI 2563 - 3454). The moose population is estimated to have 
increased by 30.4% since the 2018/19 survey, representing an annual average (geometric mean) population 
growth rate of 1.07 (90% CI 1.00-1.13). 
We also observed 1 mule deer, 47 white-tailed deer, 85 elk, 11 wolves, and 1 fisher. Of the elk observed, 38 were 
cows, 16 were calves, and 32 were bulls (15 small, 12 medium, and 4 large). Of the white -tailed deer observed, 
18 were does, 12 were fawns, and 1 antlerless buck. Note that these should not be considered minimum total 
counts as this survey method is unreliable for these species in heavily forested WMUs with lower population 
densities.
